exact_statement: For every strictly increasing sequence of positive moduli n_i and arbitrary residue classes a_i modulo n_i, determine whether the set of natural n such that for every i either n<n_i or n is not congruent to a_i modulo n_i must have a logarithmic density.
scope_notes: Continuation of erdos-25-sparse-cell-packing-longrun2-20260825; the public statement and source are unchanged.
The sole theorem-grade target is: for fixed C, determine whether every union of positive progressions r_j+d_j N_0 has logarithmic density when r_j and d_j are strictly increasing and r_j<d_j<=C r_j.
A positive solution must give an all-sequence logarithmic Cauchy or periodic-approximation bound; another finite convergent family is not enough.
A negative solution must specify one fixed infinite rule, retain certified positive inner density, and prove nonvanishing signed rises and recovery drops after logarithmic normalization.
Raw endpoint range, retuned finite champions, unsigned changes, and finite persistence are non-success conditions.
The round has a hard allocation of 14400 seconds including setup, guarded computation, mathematical synthesis, replay, and freeze or promotion review.
